stemMd: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature. During an isothermal expansion, the gas does 200 J of work. How much heat must it absorb?
explanationMd: Isothermal ideal-gas expansion has ΔU = 0. With work done by the gas positive, ΔU = Q − W implies Q = W = 200 J. Heat input exactly replaces the energy leaving as work.

distractorRationale.c: Constant temperature means zero internal-energy change, not zero heat transfer.
distractorRationale.a: Rejecting heat while doing work would lower internal energy.
distractorRationale.b: This double-counts the required energy input.
distractorRationale.d: This supplies only half the energy transferred as work.
